ports.name: items
ports.description: The list to run the template once for; each entry becomes one task and is passed to it as a record

ports.name: stopOnFailure
ports.description: Abandons the remaining items as soon as one task fails, rather than running the whole list

ports.name: maxRunningTasks
ports.description: How many tasks may run at the same time; must be at least 1 or the run fails rather than starting

ports.name: taskTemplate

ports.name: taskStartInput

ports.name: taskSuccessOutput

ports.name: taskFailureOutput

ports.name: taskErrorOutput

ports.name: abort
ports.description: Stops starting new tasks and ends the run once those already running finish; does nothing when no run is in progress

responseScript
expression

ports.name: scriptInputs

ports.name: scriptOutputs
ports.description: Names of the values the script writes to Outputs, each becoming an output port

ports.name: functionScript
ports.description: JavaScript run when Run fires, reading Inputs.name and writing Outputs.name

ports.name: run
ports.description: Runs the script now. This is additional to the inputs that re-run it; untick an input under Run On Value Change to stop that one triggering a run

ports.name: workspace
ports.description: The block program itself, authored in the block editor — it decides which ports this node has, so editing it adds and removes ports

ports.name: generatedCode
ports.description: The JavaScript the block editor writes out of Logic Blocks and the runtime actually executes; it is overwritten on every block edit, so hand edits do not survive

ports.name: run
ports.description: Runs the block program once; the blocks never run on their own, so a value arriving at an input changes nothing until this fires

ports.name: trueString
ports.description: Text published on Current Value while Selector is true

ports.name: falseString
ports.description: Text published on Current Value while Selector is false

ports.name: input
ports.description: Which of the two strings to publish; anything that is not true counts as false

ports.name: formatString
ports.description: Template in which {year} {yearShort} {month} {monthShort} {date} {hours} {minutes} {seconds} are replaced and everything else is copied through

ports.name: input
ports.description: The instant to render; a string arriving here is parsed as a date first

ports.name: inputString
ports.description: The string to look up among the numbered inputs

ports.name: defaultMapping
ports.description: Published when Input String matches none of the numbered inputs

ports.name: value
ports.description: Value to negate; anything falsy counts as false, and leaving it unset keeps Result unset too

ports.name: start
ports.description: Position of the first character to keep, counting from zero; a negative value counts back from the end

ports.name: end
ports.description: Position to stop before; leave it unset to run to the end of the string, since setting it to 0 yields nothing

ports.name: string
ports.description: Text to take the substring from; it must not be cleared to null, which raises an error rather than yielding an empty result

ports.name: format
ports.description: Template text; each {placeholder} becomes an input port, and a placeholder used twice fills only the first time

ports.name: increase
ports.description: Adds one to the count, or does nothing at all when Limits Enabled and the count is already at Max Value

ports.name: decrease
ports.description: Subtracts one from the count, or does nothing at all when Limits Enabled and the count is already at Min Value

ports.name: reset
ports.description: Puts the count back to Start Value

ports.name: startValue
ports.description: Count to begin at and to return to on Reset; setting it announces a change on Count Changed at page load

ports.name: limitsMin
ports.description: Lowest count Decrease will reach, ignored unless Limits Enabled

ports.name: limitsMax
ports.description: Highest count Increase will reach, ignored unless Limits Enabled

ports.name: limitsEnabled
ports.description: Whether Min Value and Max Value bound the count; without it the count runs unbounded in both directions

ports.name: new
ports.description: Generates a fresh id, replacing the one on Id

ports.name: filter
ports.description: Only errors whose Code starts with this text are reported; leave blank to catch every error in the app

ports.name: store
ports.description: Writes the values below to the signed-in user; does nothing at all while nobody is signed in

ports.name: email
ports.description: New email address for the signed-in user; leave blank to keep the current one

ports.name: username
ports.description: New username for the signed-in user; leave blank to keep the current one

ports.name: fetch
ports.description: Re-reads the signed-in user from the backend, which is also how an expired session is discovered

ports.name: runOnChange-user
ports.description: Whether a new value on User properties re-runs this node. On by default; untick to make this input passive so only the control signal runs it

ports.name: storeName
ports.description: Names the store this node reads; several nodes may share a name and every one of them sees the same state

ports.name: initialState
ports.description: Keys to fill in on stores that do not already have them, as an object or as JSON text; live values are never overwritten

ports.name: persist
ports.description: Keeps the store in browser storage so it survives a reload; under SSR and cloud functions there is no storage and Error says so

ports.name: storageKey
ports.description: Name to store the persisted copy under, defaulting to Store Name; ignored unless Persist is on

ports.name: storeName
ports.description: Names the store to write; must match the Store Name of the Global Store node that owns it

ports.name: key
ports.description: Key to write; a Set with no key is refused rather than dropped

ports.name: value
ports.description: Value to write, of any type; null is stored as null and is not coerced to a blank string

ports.name: merge
ports.description: Shallow-merges into the existing value when both the old and the new value are plain objects, instead of replacing it

ports.name: transaction
ports.description: Holds the notification until the end of the current microtask so several writers in one turn produce a single change

ports.name: set
ports.description: Writes Value at Key, reading both as of the end of the current frame

ports.name: storeName
ports.description: Names the store to watch; must match the Store Name of the Global Store node that owns it

ports.name: keys
ports.description: Comma-separated keys to watch; leave blank to react to every change in the store
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated keys to watch. Leave blank to react to every change in the store.

ports.name: storeName
ports.description: Names the store holding the key this update writes

ports.name: key
ports.description: Key to write optimistically; an Apply with no key is refused rather than dropped

ports.name: optimisticValue
ports.description: Value to show immediately, before the server has confirmed anything

ports.name: errorMessage
ports.description: Reason reported on Error when this update is rolled back; wire the server error here
ports.tooltip: Reason reported on Error when this update is rolled back. Wire the server error here.

ports.name: transactionId
ports.description: Names the update to commit or roll back when several are in flight; leave blank to generate one and resolve to the oldest
ports.tooltip: Leave blank to let the node generate one. Set it to commit or roll back a specific update when several are in flight.

ports.name: timeout
ports.description: Milliseconds to wait for an answer before rolling back on its own; 0 waits forever
ports.tooltip: Roll back automatically after this long with no answer. Zero disables the deadline.

ports.name: onDispose
ports.description: What happens to updates still in flight when this node is removed: put the old value back, or keep the value that was shown
ports.tooltip: What happens to updates still in flight when this node is removed. Rolling back keeps the store honest; keeping the value suits fire-and-forget actions the user navigates away from.

ports.name: apply
ports.description: Writes Optimistic Value at Key now and opens a transaction the server response will resolve

ports.name: commit
ports.description: Confirms the update, so the optimistic value becomes the truth

ports.name: rollback
ports.description: Puts the old value back, unless something else has written the key since

ports.name: storeName
ports.description: Names the global store to record; one tracker per store is enough, and two on the same store share one history

ports.name: trackKeys
ports.description: Comma-separated keys to record; leave blank to record the whole store, and note that changing this clears the history
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated keys to record. Blank records the whole store. Undo then writes only these keys and leaves the rest alone. Changing this clears the history.

ports.name: maxHistory
ports.description: How many entries to keep before the oldest is dropped, never below two and never dropping the current one
ports.tooltip: How many entries to keep. The oldest are dropped first. An unbounded history is a memory leak.

ports.name: coalesceMs
ports.description: Window in milliseconds within which successive changes to the same keys fold into one undo step; 0 records every change separately
ports.tooltip: Fold successive changes to the same keys within this many milliseconds into one undo step, so typing is one undo rather than one per keystroke. 0 records every change separately.

ports.name: enabled
ports.description: Turning this off pauses recording and keeps the entries already collected
ports.tooltip: Turning this off pauses recording. The history already collected is kept.

ports.name: clearHistory
ports.description: Throws the history away and starts again from the live state

ports.name: storeName
ports.description: Names the store to step through; a State History node must already be tracking it

ports.name: targetIndex
ports.description: Entry to move to when Jump To is signalled, counting from zero; ignored by Undo and Redo

ports.name: undo
ports.description: Steps the store back one entry, or fires Unchanged when it is already at the beginning

ports.name: redo
ports.description: Steps the store forward one entry, or fires Unchanged when it is already at the end

ports.name: jumpTo
ports.description: Moves the store to the entry named by Target Index

ports.name: storeName
ports.description: Names the store to snapshot or restore into

ports.name: snapshotName
ports.description: Name to save this checkpoint under, and the name Restore looks up; required to save

ports.name: snapshotData
ports.description: A previously exported Snapshot to restore instead of the named one; leave blank to restore by name
ports.tooltip: Snapshot to restore instead of the named one — a previously exported "Snapshot" output. Leave blank to restore by name.

ports.name: save
ports.description: Copies the store as it is now and keeps it under Snapshot Name

ports.name: restore
ports.description: Puts a checkpoint back as an ordinary write, so it appears in the history and can itself be undone

ports.name: url
ports.description: Endpoint to connect to, which must start with ws:// or wss://; changing it reconnects to the new one

ports.name: autoConnect
ports.description: Connect as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal
ports.tooltip: Connect as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal.

ports.name: protocols
ports.description: Comma-separated WebSocket subprotocols to offer during the handshake
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated WebSocket subprotocols to offer during the handshake.

ports.name: autoReconnect
ports.description: Retries after an unsolicited close with a growing backoff; turning it off reports the close as an error

ports.name: reconnectDelay
ports.description: First backoff delay in milliseconds; each further attempt doubles it up to Max Reconnect Delay
ports.tooltip: First backoff delay. Each further attempt doubles it, up to Max Reconnect Delay.

ports.name: maxReconnectDelay
ports.description: Ceiling on the backoff in milliseconds, however many attempts there have been

ports.name: maxRetries
ports.description: Reconnect attempts allowed per outage; 0 disables retrying and a negative value means unlimited
ports.tooltip: Reconnect attempts allowed per outage. 0 disables retrying; a negative value means unlimited.

ports.name: jitter
ports.description: Spreads reconnect attempts randomly across the second half of each backoff window, so a fleet does not return in lockstep
ports.tooltip: Spread reconnect attempts randomly across the second half of each backoff window.

ports.name: heartbeatInterval
ports.description: Milliseconds between heartbeats while the socket is open; 0 disables it, and only enable it if your server expects the message
ports.tooltip: Send Heartbeat Message this often while open. 0 disables it. Only enable this if your server expects the message — it is application data, not a protocol ping frame.

ports.name: heartbeatMessage
ports.description: Application text sent as the heartbeat; it is not a protocol ping frame

ports.name: heartbeatReply
ports.description: Exact text the server answers a heartbeat with; it is measured as Latency, hidden from On Message, and its absence is treated as a dead connection
ports.tooltip: Exact text the server answers a heartbeat with. It is measured as Latency, hidden from On Message, and — if it stops arriving — treated as a dead connection. Leave empty to only send heartbeats.

ports.name: connect
ports.description: Opens the socket, replacing one already open without reporting a close

ports.name: disconnect
ports.description: Closes the socket and cancels any pending reconnect

ports.name: send
ports.description: Hands the current Message to the socket, or applies the When Disconnected policy

ports.name: message
ports.description: Value to send; objects are JSON-serialised, and ArrayBuffers and typed arrays go as binary frames
ports.tooltip: Value to send. Objects are JSON-serialized; ArrayBuffers and typed arrays are sent as binary frames.

ports.name: messageType
ports.description: Auto sends binary values as binary and everything else as text; Binary encodes text and objects as UTF-8 first
ports.tooltip: Auto sends binary values as binary and everything else as text. Binary forces text and objects to be UTF-8 encoded first.

ports.name: whenDisconnected
ports.description: What a Send does while the socket is not open: hold it in order, discard and count it, or also report an error
ports.tooltip: What a Send does while the connection is not open. Queue holds it (in order) until the socket reopens; Drop discards it and counts it; Report Error also sets Last Error and fires On Error.

ports.name: maxQueueSize
ports.description: Messages the queue holds before further Sends are refused and counted as dropped; 0 or less is unlimited and can grow during a long outage
ports.tooltip: Messages the queue holds before further Sends are refused and counted in Dropped. 0 or less means unlimited, which can grow without bound during a long outage.

ports.name: url
ports.description: Endpoint to stream from; changing it while connected reconnects to the new one

ports.name: transport
ports.description: How the stream is fetched: Fetch carries headers and a body, EventSource lets the browser handle reconnection, Auto prefers Fetch

ports.name: method
ports.description: HTTP method for the request; anything other than GET needs the Fetch transport

ports.name: headers
ports.description: Request headers as an object, for bearer tokens and the like; ignored by the EventSource transport, which cannot set them

ports.name: body
ports.description: Request body, sent as JSON unless it is already a string; ignored for GET and HEAD

ports.name: withCredentials
ports.description: Sends cookies and HTTP auth to a cross-origin endpoint, which the server must also allow

ports.name: eventTypes
ports.description: Comma-separated named event types to subscribe to; only needed for the EventSource transport, as Fetch delivers every type
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated named event types to subscribe to. Only needed for the EventSource transport, which delivers a named event only to a listener registered in advance; the Fetch transport delivers every event type.

ports.name: textPath
ports.description: Where the text lives inside a JSON payload, as a dot path such as choices.0.delta.content; leave blank for a stream of bare text
ports.tooltip: Where the text lives inside a JSON payload, as a dot path — for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, choices.0.delta.content. Leave blank for a stream that sends bare text. Whatever it names ends up on the Text output, which is always a string.

ports.name: autoConnect
ports.description: Opens the stream as soon as a URL is available, without waiting for a Connect signal

ports.name: autoReconnect
ports.description: Retries after a failure with a growing backoff; turning it off reports the failure and stops

ports.name: reconnectOnStreamEnd
ports.description: Reconnects when the server closes the stream cleanly; off by default because reconnecting an agent stream re-issues the request
ports.tooltip: Reconnect when the server closes the stream cleanly. Off by default: an agent response stream is finite, and reconnecting would re-issue the request and start the response again.

ports.name: reconnectDelay
ports.description: First retry delay in milliseconds, doubling per consecutive failure up to Max Reconnect Delay
ports.tooltip: First retry delay. Doubles per consecutive failure, up to the maximum.

ports.name: maxReconnectDelay
ports.description: Ceiling on the backoff in milliseconds, however many failures there have been

ports.name: maxRetries
ports.description: Consecutive failures allowed before the connection gives up and reports an error; 0 keeps retrying
ports.tooltip: 0 means keep retrying. Otherwise the connection reports an error after this many consecutive failures.

ports.name: dedupeById
ports.description: Drops events whose id has already been seen, so a reconnect that resumes cannot re-deliver messages
ports.tooltip: Drop events whose id has already been seen, so a reconnect that resumes from the last event id cannot re-deliver messages. Turn off if your server reuses ids for distinct events.

ports.name: connect
ports.description: Opens the stream, replacing any connection already open and resetting the retry count

ports.name: disconnect
ports.description: Closes the stream and stops retrying

ports.name: chunk
ports.description: The next fragment of text to append; wire a stream Text output, not its Data output, which is JSON-parsed and is usually an object

ports.name: delimiter
ports.description: Message boundary to split complete messages off; leave empty to accumulate everything, which is what a token stream wants
ports.tooltip: Message boundary. Leave empty to accumulate everything without splitting — the mode a token stream wants.

ports.name: maxLength
ports.description: Cap on the pending buffer in characters; overflow drops the oldest and is counted on Dropped Characters
ports.tooltip: Cap on the pending buffer. Overflow drops the oldest characters and is reported on Dropped Characters.

ports.name: maxMessages
ports.description: Cap on retained complete messages, oldest dropped first; 0 keeps them all, which grows forever
ports.tooltip: Cap on retained complete messages; the oldest are dropped first. 0 keeps them all, which grows forever.

ports.name: add
ports.description: Appends the current Chunk, which is retained between pulses, so a second Add with no new chunk appends it again

ports.name: clear
ports.description: Empties the buffer, the messages and both dropped counts

ports.name: chunk
ports.description: The next fragment of the stream; boundaries may fall anywhere, including inside a string

ports.name: format
ports.description: How values are framed on this stream: one per line, any concatenation of complete values, or one whole document

ports.name: maxLength
ports.description: Cap on unparsed text held while a value completes; exceeding it clears the buffer and reports an error rather than growing forever
ports.tooltip: Cap on unparsed text held while waiting for a value to complete. Exceeding it clears the buffer and reports an error, rather than growing without limit on a malformed stream.

ports.name: parse
ports.description: Appends the current Chunk and emits every value that is now complete; the chunk is retained between pulses

ports.name: clear
ports.description: Discards the pending text, the parsed values and the error counter

ports.name: text
ports.description: The text to search

ports.name: pattern
ports.description: A JavaScript regular expression without the surrounding slashes; capture groups appear on Groups
ports.tooltip: A JavaScript regular expression, without the surrounding slashes. Capture groups appear on Groups.

ports.name: flags
ports.description: Regex flags i, m, s, u and y; g is controlled by Extract All and a g written here is ignored
ports.tooltip: Regex flags: i (ignore case), m (multiline), s (dot matches newline), u (unicode). g is controlled by Extract All.

ports.name: extractAll
ports.description: Collects every match into Matches instead of stopping at the first one

ports.name: extract
ports.description: Runs Pattern over Text and reports what it found

ports.name: data
ports.description: The next item to buffer, of any type; its value is retained between pulses of Add

ports.name: flushSize
ports.description: Flush automatically once this many items are buffered; 0 disables size-based flushing
ports.tooltip: Flush automatically once this many items are buffered. 0 disables size-based flushing.

ports.name: flushInterval
ports.description: Flush automatically this often in milliseconds while items are buffered; 0 disables interval flushing
ports.tooltip: Flush automatically this often while items are buffered. 0 disables interval flushing.

ports.name: maxSize
ports.description: Hard cap on buffered items; overflow drops the oldest and is counted on Dropped Items; 0 means no cap
ports.tooltip: Hard cap on buffered items. Overflow drops the oldest and is reported on Dropped Items. 0 means no cap.

ports.name: add
ports.description: Buffers the current Data, flushing straight away if that reaches Flush Size

ports.name: flush
ports.description: Hands the whole buffer to Flushed Data now; an empty buffer is a legitimate no-op

ports.name: clear
ports.description: Discards the buffer and resets both counters without flushing

ports.name: channel
ports.description: Names the handler registry this dispatcher draws on; leave it as default unless two independent flows must not see each other
ports.tooltip: Names the handler registry this dispatcher draws on. Leave as "default" unless two independent flows must not see each other.

ports.name: action
ports.description: An action object, an array of them to run in order, or JSON text holding either
ports.tooltip: An action object, an array of them to run in order, or JSON text holding either.

ports.name: builtIns
ports.description: Comma-separated built-in action names this dispatcher may execute; empty, the default, means a server cannot write to the store at all
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated built-in action names this dispatcher may execute: SET_STORE, MERGE_STORE, DELETE_STORE_KEY, CLEAR_STORE. Empty — the default — means a server cannot write to the store at all; everything must go through an Action Handler you wired.

ports.name: storeName
ports.description: The only store the built-in actions can write; a store named inside an incoming action is ignored
ports.tooltip: The only store the built-in actions can write. A store named inside an incoming action is ignored — the graph chooses the store, not the server.

ports.name: allowedKeys
ports.description: Comma-separated keys the built-in store actions may write; blank means any key, and setting any key also refuses CLEAR_STORE
ports.tooltip: Comma-separated keys the built-in store actions may write. Blank means any key of the configured store. Setting any key also refuses CLEAR_STORE.

ports.name: handlerTimeout
ports.description: Milliseconds a handler has to signal Complete or Fail before the action is failed; 0 waits forever
ports.tooltip: How long a handler has to signal Complete or Fail before the action is failed. 0 waits forever.

ports.name: waitForHandler
ports.description: Milliseconds an action waits for its handler to appear before being refused as unknown; everything behind it waits too
ports.tooltip: How long an action waits for its handler to appear before being refused as unknown — the window in which a component can still mount. 0 refuses immediately. Everything behind it waits too, because order is preserved.

ports.name: maxQueueSize
ports.description: Bound on queued actions; overflow refuses the newest so accepted actions keep their order; 0 is unbounded
ports.tooltip: Bound on queued actions. Overflow refuses the newest so accepted actions keep their order. 0 is unbounded.

ports.name: rateLimit
ports.description: Actions executed per window before the rest are refused rather than delayed; 0 is unlimited
ports.tooltip: Max actions executed per window. 0 is unlimited. Excess actions are refused, not delayed.

ports.name: rateLimitWindow
ports.description: Length of the rate-limit window in milliseconds; ignored unless Rate Limit is set

ports.name: dispatch
ports.description: Admits whatever is on Action and runs it, or refuses it with a reason

ports.name: cancel
ports.description: Discards everything queued and abandons anything in flight, reporting how many were dropped

ports.name: channel
ports.description: Must match the Channel on the Action Dispatcher that should be able to reach this handler
ports.tooltip: Must match the Channel on the Action Dispatcher that should be able to reach this handler.

ports.name: actionType
ports.description: The exact action type this handler accepts; registering it is what makes it executable at all
ports.tooltip: The exact action type this handler accepts, e.g. OPEN_SESSION. Registering it is what makes it executable at all.

ports.name: enabled
ports.description: Turning this off unregisters the handler, so the action is refused as unknown rather than quietly ignored
ports.tooltip: Turning this off unregisters the handler, so the action is refused as unknown rather than quietly ignored.

ports.name: autoComplete
ports.description: Reports the action complete as soon as Trigger has been sent; turn it off when a later step must finish first
ports.tooltip: Report the action complete as soon as Trigger has been sent. Turn off when a later step must wait for this one to finish, and wire Complete or Fail yourself.

ports.name: result
ports.description: Handed back to the dispatcher as the Result of this action when it completes
ports.tooltip: Handed back to the dispatcher as the Result of this action when it completes.

ports.name: errorMessage
ports.description: Reason handed back to the dispatcher when Fail is signalled; a generic one is used when this is blank

ports.name: complete
ports.description: Reports the action finished, so the dispatcher runs whatever is queued behind it; ignored unless Auto Complete is off

ports.name: fail
ports.description: Reports the action failed, so the dispatcher fires Failed with Error Message as the reason

ports.name: allowNoAuth
ports.description: Whether a request with no valid session token is allowed to run this function at all

ports.name: params
ports.description: Names to pull out of the request body, each becoming an output

dynamicports.name: conditionalports/extended
dynamicports.condition: status = success OR status NOT SET

ports.name: params
ports.description: Names to return in the response body, each becoming an input to supply it

ports.name: errorMessage
ports.description: Message returned to the caller; used only when Status is Failure

ports.name: params
ports.description: Names to return in the response body, each becoming an input to supply it

ports.name: errorMessage
ports.description: Message returned to the caller; used only when Status is Failure

ports.name: send
ports.description: Sends the response and ends the request, which can only happen once

ports.name: status
ports.description: Whether the caller gets a 200 carrying Parameters or a 400 carrying Error Message

ports.name: to
ports.description: Address the message goes to; the send fails outright when this is blank

ports.name: template
ports.description: Which stored template to render, or None to use Subject, Text Body and HTML Body instead

ports.name: variables
ports.description: Values substituted into the template placeholders, and ignored when Template is None

ports.name: subject
ports.description: Subject line of the message, and ignored when Template is set

ports.name: text
ports.description: Plain-text body of the message, and ignored when Template is set

ports.name: html
ports.description: HTML body sent alongside Text Body; optional, and ignored when Template is set

ports.name: send
ports.description: Sends the message

ports.name: aggregates
ports.description: Names of the aggregates to compute, each of which gets its own property and operation inputs

coreNodes.name: Cloud Functions
coreNodes.description: Nodes to be used in cloud functions
